Sparky

- An Ender 3 Pro, gradually rebuilt.

Sparky is the Ender 3 Pro I bought in 2019. It has printed parts for much of the work on this site. I keep upgrading the same machine because each change leaves me with a printer I understand better.

Control

  • Klipper and MainsailOS on a Raspberry Pi 4B
  • Tailscale remote access
  • Creality 4.2.7 controller board
  • Logitech camera aimed at the build plate

Motion and toolhead

  • X- and Y-axis linear rails
  • X- and Y-axis belt tensioners salvaged from an Ender 3 V2
  • Low-profile KevinAkaSam dual-belted-Z conversion (with V-rollers)
  • Creality Sprite Pro direct-drive all-metal hot end
  • Taurus V5 part cooling with two 24 V 5015 blowers

Bed and cooling

  • PEI build surface
  • CR Touch bed probe
  • Creality silicone bed spacers
  • Noctua hot-end, mainboard and power-supply fans
  • Printed PSU fan face and offset mount, keeping it vertical and clear of the frame
  • Upgrade parts printed in white PETG

Calibration

  • Two ADXL345s stay mounted: one on the Sprite Pro, one on the bed
  • One SPI lead moves between them for X/Y resonance tests, then comes off before printing
  • Input shaping comes from accelerometer sweeps; pressure advance from calibration prints
